correctness.rationale: The stationary Gaussian variance-mixture integral converges because gamma+(lambda/s)log(1-s)<0. Splitting at the first backward Poisson point yields an explicit positive perpetuity; Kesten–Goldie hypotheses (nonarithmetic log A, positive B, Elog A<0, E A^rho=1, finite rho+epsilon B moment, strict nondegeneracy) hold and Breiman supplies the physical tail. The approximate stationary density is Galla Eq.(5) at alpha=0. Taylor remainder sign about exponent 2 proves the exhaustive strict comparison. Exact generators give matching second moment and distinct fourth-moment barriers. The weak-reset c_b equation has a unique strictly positive root and the implicit expansion is regular. 607 deterministic checks passed; these do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The full finite-amplitude phase diagram identifies exactly where Gaussianizing frequent contractions gives a lighter or heavier inferred rare-event exponent. Both models have identical finite variances, yet a natural open parameter wedge has exact finite fourth moment versus approximate infinite fourth moment, a qualitative failure for tail-sensitive observables. The singular ratio c_b/[2(1-b)]>1 shows the discrepancy survives arbitrarily weak resets in far-tail scaling. This is motivated by accuracy of the source diffusion approximation, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
